carousels.name: Your p*rn recovery isn't a leaderboard

slides.title: Someone's on Day 300. You're on Day 3. [[Quitting p*rn isn't a race.]]
slides.sub: Why comparing streaks can hurt your recovery.

slides.title: The [[comparison]] trap
slides.body: Scrolling other people's p*rn-free streaks can make your own progress feel worthless. That feeling pushes people toward relapse, not away from it.

slides.title: You don't see their [[story]]
slides.body: Their triggers, their past, their support — all different from yours. Day 3 after 10 years of p*rn is a big deal.

slides.title: Compete with [[yesterday]]
slides.body: The only fair comparison: you vs. you last month. Fewer p*rn urges? Faster bounce-back? That's progress.

slides.title: Use community [[right]]
items: Mute anything that makes you feel behind.
slides.note: What day are you on? Every number is welcome here 👇

carousels.name: P*rn addiction in your 20s: the decade it steals

slides.title: Your 20s are too important [[to lose to p*rn.]]
slides.sub: The decade you build everything — don't spend it alone with a screen.

slides.title: The [[building]] decade
slides.body: Career, friendships, relationships, health, confidence — most of it gets built in your 20s. P*rn addiction quietly takes hours from all of it.

slides.title: Real life feels [[harder]]
slides.body: Dating, risk, rejection — real life is messy. P*rn is easy. That's exactly why it can keep you from the real thing.

slides.title: Habits [[harden]]
slides.body: The p*rn habits you build at 22 tend to follow you to 32. The earlier you quit, the easier it usually is.

slides.title: Invest your 20s [[instead]]
items: Your skills: one thing you get paid for.
Your mind: quit p*rn and get clear.
slides.note: How old are you, and when did you decide to quit p*rn? 👇

carousels.name: Reading about p*rn addiction isn't recovery

slides.title: You've watched 50 videos about quitting p*rn. [[Have you blocked it yet?]]
slides.sub: Learning feels like progress. It isn't — until you act.

slides.title: Research [[mode]]
slides.body: Reading, watching, saving posts about p*rn addiction feels productive. But it can become a way to avoid actually changing.

slides.title: Knowledge isn't [[action]]
slides.body: You already know enough to start: block p*rn, know your triggers, tell someone. The missing piece is doing it.

slides.title: One action [[beats]] ten posts
slides.body: Installing a p*rn blocker today does more than reading ten more carousels. Including this one.

slides.title: Do [[one]] thing now
items: Install a p*rn blocker on your phone.
Delete one app that leads you to p*rn.
slides.note: Which one are you doing right now? Comment it when it's done ✅

slides.title: Did you choose your "type" — or [[did p*rn choose it for you?]]
slides.sub: How p*rn can shape what you find attractive.

slides.title: Repetition [[shapes]] taste
slides.body: What you watch over and over can shape what excites you. Years of p*rn means years of training your attraction.

slides.title: Real people [[don't match]]
slides.body: Many men in recovery say p*rn left them less drawn to real partners — who don't look or act like a screen. That gap can hurt real relationships.

slides.title: It can [[shift]] back
slides.body: Many people describe their attraction to real people growing after time away from p*rn. Everyone's different — but change is common.

slides.title: Reconnect with [[real]] attraction
items: Spend time with real people, in real places.
slides.note: Has quitting p*rn changed what you find attractive? 👇
